study_material.title: Coding - Decoding - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Coding-decoding questions give a word and its code, and ask you to apply the same rule elsewhere. The rules are almost always letter shifts, reversals, positional values or substitution - find the rule, apply it mechanically.
learning_objectives: Handle reversal and opposite-letter (A-Z pairing) codes
Decode number and symbol substitution ciphers

concepts.heading: 1. Letter Shifts
concepts.body: Each letter moves a fixed number of steps: CAT to DBU is +1, TIGER to QFDBO is -3. Write the alphabet positions above the letters and compare. Check two or three letters before trusting the rule.

concepts.heading: 2. Position Values
concepts.body: A=1, B=2 ... Z=26. Codes may sum positions (CAB = 3+1+2 = 6), multiply, or use reverse positions (A=26 ... Z=1, i.e. reverse of letter x = 27 - x). Memorise EJOTY: E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Y=25 as anchors.

concepts.heading: 3. Reversal and Opposites
concepts.body: Reversal codes write the word backwards. Opposite-letter codes map A to Z, B to Y (positions summing to 27). Mixed rules exist: reverse then shift. Test the simplest rule first.

concepts.heading: 4. Substitution Codes
concepts.body: Words or symbols stand for other words ('sky is called sea, sea is called water...'). Follow the chain literally - the answer is what the coded language calls the real-world item, not the real name.

formulas: Shift k: letter -> letter + k (wrap around after Z)
Reverse letter of x = 27 - x position
shortcut_methods: Verify the rule on at least two letters
For long words, decode only the letters needed to pick an option
Write positions under letters - errors vanish when you compute on paper
common_mistakes: Assuming a +k shift after checking only one letter
Forgetting the wrap-around from Z to A
Answering the real name instead of the coded name in substitution puzzles
study_material.summary: Compare letter positions, deduce the rule, verify twice, apply once - and in substitution chains answer within the coded language.
quick_revision_notes: Substitution: answer in the coded vocabulary

solved_examples.question: If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded?
solved_examples.step_by_step: Each letter shifts +1: D->E, O->P, G->H.

solved_examples.question: If TIGER is written as QFDBO, how is LION written?
solved_examples.step_by_step: The rule is -3: L->I, I->F, O->L, N->K.

solved_examples.question: If A=1, B=2 ... Z=26, what is the code value of the word BEAD (sum of positions)?
In a code, 'sky is called sea, sea is called water, water is called air'. Where do fish live (answer in the code)?
solved_examples.step_by_step: Fish live in sea (real). The code calls sea 'water'.
solved_examples.shortcut: Trace exactly one link of the chain.
